content.text: I've read the brief against the release line by line. Findings below.

facts.evidence: Total revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $60.80 billion, representing a 28% increase year-over-year
diluted earnings per share declined 13% to $6.18
operating income for this segment fell to $23.39 billion from $24.97 billion in the prior year
Operating income decreased to $18.78 billion from $20.44 billion in the prior year, resulting in an operating margin of 31% compared to 43% previously.
The company expects third quarter 2026 total revenue to be between $61 billion and $64 billion
Total costs and expenses rose 55% year-over-year to $42.03 billion
a $2.40 billion charge for legal proceedings and $1.18 billion in severance expenses related to the May 2026 headcount reduction

Free cash flow for the quarter was $784 million, calculated by subtracting purchases of property and equipment ($30.12 billion) and principal payments on finance leases ($962 million) from operating cash flow.
Capital expenditures for full year 2026 are expected to be between $130 billion and $145 billion, narrowed from the prior outlook of $125 billion to $145 billion.
Family daily active people (DAP) averaged 3.60 billion, a 3% increase year-over-year

claims.claim: Total revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $60.80 billion.
Revenue increased 28% year over year.
On a constant currency basis, revenue increased 27% year over year.
Net income was $15.85 billion.
Net income was down 14% from the prior-year period.
Diluted earnings per share was $6.18, a 13% decline year over year.
Total costs and expenses rose 55% year over year to $42.03 billion.
Costs and expenses included a $2.40 billion charge related to legal proceedings.
Costs and expenses included $1.18 billion of severance expenses related to the May 2026 headcount reduction.
The 55% increase in total costs and expenses was driven by the $2.40 billion legal charge and the $1.18 billion severance expense.
claims.note: The release only says total costs 'includes' these items; it attributes no causation. The two items total ~$3.58B against a ~$14.95B year-over-year cost increase, so 'driven by' is not supported without calculation.

claims.claim: Operating income decreased to $18.78 billion from $20.44 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Operating margin was 31%, compared with 43% in the prior-year quarter.
Family daily active people averaged 3.60 billion, a 3% increase year over year.
Ad impressions grew 14% year over year.
Average price per ad increased 12% year over year.
Advertising revenue was $59.36 billion in the quarter.
Family of Apps segment revenue was $60.37 billion in the quarter.
Family of Apps operating income fell to $23.39 billion from $24.97 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Reality Labs revenue was $431 million in the quarter.
Reality Labs operating loss was $4.62 billion in the quarter.
Reality Labs cumulative six-month losses widened slightly to $8.65 billion from $8.74 billion in the prior-year period.
claims.note: Contradicts the release: the six-month Reality Labs loss narrowed, from $8,739 million in 2025 to $8,647 million in 2026. The brief's own figures show a smaller loss but describe it as 'widening.'

claims.claim: Meta expects third quarter 2026 total revenue of $61 billion to $64 billion.
The revenue guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year growth.
Full year 2026 total expenses are projected at $165 billion to $169 billion.
The expense outlook was raised from prior guidance to incorporate the second quarter legal charges.
Full year 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be $130 billion to $145 billion, narrowed from a prior outlook of $125 billion to $145 billion.
Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $90.26 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Long-term debt increased to $83.66 billion from $58.74 billion at year-end 2025.
Free cash flow for the quarter was $784 million.
Free cash flow was derived by subtracting purchases of property and equipment of $30.12 billion and principal payments on finance leases of $962 million from operating cash flow.
The company paid $1.35 billion of dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter.
Operating margins compressed significantly despite revenue growth.
Reality Labs continues to generate substantial losses.
Reality Labs has limited revenue growth.
claims.note: The release does not characterize Reality Labs revenue growth; the segment table shows revenue rose from $370 million to $431 million year over year (about 16%), a comparison the release does not compute or describe.

claims.claim: Reported headcount includes approximately 8,000 employees impacted by the May 2026 reduction who will no longer be reflected in headcount by the end of the third quarter.
claims.note: The release says only 'the majority of whom' will no longer be reflected by the end of Q3 2026, not all ~8,000. The release also does not attribute the headcount reduction to Reality Labs, as the brief's surrounding sentence implies.

claims.claim: Management highlighted ongoing scrutiny on youth-related issues and youth-related trials scheduled in the U.S. that may ultimately result in a material loss.
